read_sentence_candidates.source: A unit is one task row or tasks that name each other in Joins, as [Work Breakdown](epic-issue-body.md#work-breakdown) defines. A unit of rows comes only from an epic that is Ready or In Progress in the supplied board items: the plan offers no other row, and none other is held. A [hot-fix unit](#hot-fix-units) has no row. One unit is one session's work, delivered by one pull request into each epic base it changes. Its first task id and Description determine the planning-folder identity, which every row of the unit is reserved with, and with each epic base it changes its branch and worktree, as [Task Branches](delivery-branches.md#task-branches) names them. In an epic of several bases, the bases a unit changes are read from the [Component](work-item.md#component) declaration of the work-item file each free row links, in the engineering worktree. A unit with a row linking no work item changes every epic base, as [Task Branches](delivery-branches.md#task-branches) states for unplanned rows.
read_sentence_candidates.reason: Describes record/source completeness, placement or evidence order rather than mandatory document loading.
read_sentence_candidates.disposition: Retain at the owning contract; do not infer transitive context closure from the sentence alone.

read_sentence_candidates.source: Check one selected unit immediately before execution and provide [Validated Unit](#validated-unit "●") to the requester, or [Failure](#failure "●") if the operation fails. The start names one selected unit, has a currently free harness slot and overlaps no held or running session. Its supplied evidence names that unit, the planning record confirmed on the remote engineering branch, and the record associated with its confirmed hold. For rows, that association is read from every live row reservation; for a hot-fix it is the run's record for the unit whose board hold was confirmed. The evidence is gathered in that order before execution; any missing, mismatched or unverified evidence blocks the start.
